This snip adds a subtle transition to your expandos on your subverse. It fades in ever so slightly when expanded, so you may not even notice it, but it gives it more of a smooth style. It is implemented here when you press the + button to see the post. Just add it to the bottom of your CSS to implement.

This works in Chrome and IE, but I haven't tested on Firefox.

/* Adjust the expanded submission box a little and
 * add some animation to fit with the site.
 * This is when you click the plus button and the box
 * with the message expands. This is just the box that
 * has the message in it.
 */
@-webkit-keyframes fadeIn {
 from { opacity: 0; }
 to { opacity: 1; }
}

@keyframes fadeIn {
 from { opacity: 0; }
 to { opacity: 1; }
}
.expando {
 padding-right: 10px;
 -webkit-animation: fadeIn .2s;
 animation: fadeIn .2s;
}

How long can one marinate red meat?
I think it should be fine. Does it pass the smell test? As long as there is no foul smell I'd go for it.
This chart is what I usually go by, as well as what my foods teacher told us in high school: When in doubt, throw it out!

This is a tiny bit off topic, but as someone has managed to answer your original question, I won't bore you with hearing that again. I'd like to say, though, that I actually wouldn't marinate meat that long (all day or all night). I tried to find a reference to the episode of Good Eats online, but of course I can't even remember the name of it. Regardless, I recall Alton Brown said that it really only takes a few hours for the marinade to penetrate as far into the meat as it's going to. He had one piece that had been marinating for about 4-8 hours, and then another that had been marinating for at least twelve, and there was no difference in how marinated the two pieces of meat were. Basically it goes a certain distance into the tissue and stops no matter what, so there's no need to leave it marinating for a long, long time. Another concern is the fact that the meat that is marinated sort of starts to break down way too much and loses quality.
